readable_sections.title: What must stay hidden
readable_sections.body:
The underlying secret is the full fixed-weight polynomial \(r\), hidden by the rounded product \(c_0=\operatorname{Round}(hr)\). For the exact research key distribution, a classical recovery attack on the complete shared key can be converted to a recovery attack on this polynomial, apart from a small hash-guessing term.

The statement is conditional on the two premises below. It does not assign a numerical hardness level: the small stages deliberately have easy instances. It covers one fresh honest challenge and public computation, without a decapsulation oracle.

readable_sections.title: From the hidden polynomial to the shared key
readable_sections.body:
Write \(\epsilon_{\rm core}(T)\) for recovery probability at a stated core-attack budget, and let \(Q\) bound all relevant classical hash queries. In the stated oracle model, the complete-key recovery probability satisfies
\[\Pr[\widehat K=K]\le \min\{1,\epsilon_{\rm core}(T_B)+(2Q+1)2^{-256}\}.\]
The reduction budget \(T_B\) includes the attacker, oracle simulation and public candidate checks. Full text gives the first-query argument and exact framing. This is a passive key-recovery result; it makes no CCA, quantum-query or side-channel claim.

These inequalities are in the stated oracle model. A concrete-implementation claim must add the separate hash-transfer slack \(\delta_{\rm hash}\) and cap the result at one.

readable_sections.title: Unconditional honest agreement by exact lifting
readable_sections.body:
For every registered tuple, honest successful generation gives exact agreement without a hardness or hash-randomness premise. In the integer ring \(\mathbb Z[x]/(x^p-x-1)\), rounding introduces ternary \(m\) and
\[3fc=3fm+gr\pmod q,\qquad \|3fm+gr\|_\infty\le8w<q/2.\]
The centered lift is therefore exact. Reducing modulo 3 removes \(3fm\), and multiplication by the stored inverse of \(g\) recovers the original \(r\). Both parties then evaluate identical deterministic encodings and hashes.

“Unconditional” concerns the specified mathematical honest experiment, conditioned on valid successful key generation. It is not a proof that arbitrary native code is bug-free or immune to timing leakage.

readable_sections.title: The hybrid-inclusive classical reference
readable_sections.body:
Fourteen configurations have references from a pinned reproduction of the authors'2020 classical sieving/free-memory model, including non-hybrid, simple-hybrid and meet-in-the-middle-hybrid routes. The first 13 small configurations remain uncalibrated.

The endpoint reference is about 129.233 modeled work bits. It is the best result in a bounded search, not a certified best-attack cost. The exact input count \(2^w\binom pw\) counts candidate re-encryptions; it is not measured in Core-SVP work units. Two intermediate configurations lie outside the 25 default navigation stages and retain their own identities.

readable_sections.title: The assumptions inside the comparison
readable_sections.body:
The estimator uses heuristic nearest-plane success and an upstream rotation/equivalence approximation. Finite search ranges and free-memory accounting define the comparison's scope. These are dependencies and declared resource conventions of the reported attack analysis; they are not a premise that no faster attack exists.

Dual, structural, quantum, multi-target and implementation attacks are outside this comparison. Finding one of them may improve the best known attack without invalidating the analyzed hybrid attack. A changed success model can change its own estimate. Quantum costs need an independently stated model; halving a classical exponent is not justified.

readable_sections.title: Rounded-product inversion
readable_sections.body:
A ternary polynomial has degree below \(p\) and coefficients in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). Uniform weight \(w\) means a uniformly chosen \(w\)-element support and independent uniform signs on that support. Uniform \(g\) means independent uniform ternary coefficients, with rejection until it is invertible in \(R/3R\). The valid parameter domain excludes \(q=3\); the field condition and \(f\ne0\) make \(3f\) invertible in \(R/qR\).

To define rounding exactly, lift each coefficient to \([-(q-1)/2,(q-1)/2]\) and subtract its representative in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) modulo \(3\). The challenge includes canonical encodings of \(h\) and the resulting rounded polynomial. Winning means returning the sampled polynomial \(r\), not merely a small vector, the secret key, or a distinguishing bit. Probability is over all displayed draws and the algorithm's coins. All attacker preprocessing, candidate generation and checks count toward \(T\).

This is a concrete family of inversion claims. It is not hardness for a uniformly random public polynomial: \(h\) has the structured quotient distribution above. Neither ring irreducibility nor a failure-free decoder establishes the claimed inversion bound.

### Use in this construction

The exact binding is release `sntrup@3`, including its 27 registered configurations and 25 default stages. Its research samplers use coefficient rejection and uniform support/sign sampling; they are not silently identified with every upstream seeded implementation. `scripts/build_ntru_frontier.py` and `crucible/ntru_reference.py` specify the retained sampling and arithmetic. The parameter table in `docs/ntru-parameter-frontier.txt` fixes \((p,q,w)\).

The separate lifting argument uses \(q\ge16w+1\), hence \(8w<q/2\), to prove exact honest input recovery. It introduces no additional unproved correctness premise for these configurations. The security argument uses the inversion bound at the reduction's total budget \(T_B\), which includes its candidate checks; an attack-estimator number is not substituted for that bound. Small configurations may be easy.

The [NTRU Prime specification](https://ntruprime.cr.yp.to/nist/ntruprime-20201007/Supporting_Documentation/doc.pdf) defines the core construction and rounding. This exact research distribution and the local passive-key reduction remain separately identified draft claims.

readable_sections.title: Domain-separated hash transfer
readable_sections.body:
Each \(b\) is one byte and \([0{:}32]\) takes the first 32 output bytes. All variable fields use the specified unambiguous encodings. A random function returns a fresh uniform 256-bit value on each new input and the same value on repeated inputs. The same core experiment and declared algorithm/resource class are compared; only the three designated hash roles change. The public \(h_4(P)\) role and core arithmetic remain concrete. \(Q\) includes all designated calls, including pre-challenge computation, and \(T\) includes all other computation.

This is a one-sided transfer claim for this key-recovery experiment and its declared core distribution. It does not assert that anyone given the algorithm of SHA-512 cannot distinguish it from a fresh random function. A fixed public hash is not literally random, and domain separation alone does not prove the transfer inequality. Keeping \(\delta_{\rm hash}\) explicit prevents an ideal-model theorem from becoming a concrete numerical guarantee.

Here “best” is a supremum over the declared uniform classical bit-RAM algorithm class, including its work and query limits. The real and ideal suprema may be attained or approached by different algorithms. This is not the stronger claim that each individual program has the same real/ideal success. The model comparison must use compatible conventions for preprocessing, available public information and hash-call accounting.

### Use in this construction

The core distribution is precisely the rounded-product experiment in this note: \(P=\operatorname{Encode}(g/(3f))\), \(c_0=\operatorname{Encode}(\operatorname{Round}_q(hr))\), and \(U=\operatorname{SmallEncode}\). The actual transform is implemented in `crucible/ntru_reference.py` and follows the [NTRU Prime specification](https://ntruprime.cr.yp.to/nist/ntruprime-20201007/Supporting_Documentation/doc.pdf).

The separately written passive classical theorem bounds the ideal success by \(\min\{1,\epsilon_{\rm core}(T_B)+(2Q+1)2^{-256}\}\). The concrete claim must retain the additional \(\delta_{\rm hash}(T,Q)\), capped at one. This premise neither supplies that slack nor proves chosen-ciphertext or quantum security. It applies to every exact profile of `sntrup@3`; it is not needed by the algebraic correctness proof.

readable_sections.title: One common measure of attack work
readable_sections.body:
These curves use **Classical bit-RAM v1**: elementary Boolean operations and one-bit memory transfers share a fixed accounting rule. All attack setup is charged to one fresh challenge. Memory capacity is unlimited in this abstraction, and the storage bound remains visible beside the graph.

The plotted quantity is \(\log_2 W\), where \(W\) bounds a specified strategy's work and its stated assumptions imply at least **50% probability of recovering the complete shared key**. These are reproducible **baseline upper bounds**, not the cheapest known attacks or a security lower bound. A bigger value does not establish a more secure scheme. Full text contains the cost rules, proofs, parameter table and reproduction commands.

readable_sections.title: Fixed-weight input enumeration
readable_sections.body: Enumerate every allowed fixed-weight ternary encapsulation input, reproduce the rounded polynomial and confirmation hash, then derive the shared key. Perfect message recovery makes this complete search unambiguous. Lattice and hybrid attacks can be much faster than this baseline.

hqc@modeled-research-v3.title: HQC: guaranteed small stages and conditional tails
hqc@modeled-research-v3.summary: Sixty-six configurations retain the August 2025 construction. The first four have a support proof; later stages use explicit probabilistic transfer premises.

sections.title: The hidden message behind a fresh challenge
sections.body:
The native encryption core hides a uniform 128-bit message \(m\) in its quasi-cyclic noisy ciphertext. The KEM derives both the key and encryption coins from a domain-separated hash of the public-key digest, \(m\), and a public salt.

A complete passive key-recovery argument can use the exact native core’s message-recovery hardness directly. It keeps the real seeded and slightly biased samplers in that problem; it does not silently replace them with independent ideal samples. The two premises below give the precise conditional statement.

sections.title: From one-way encryption to shared-key recovery
sections.body:
Let \(\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T)\) bound recovery of the uniform native message from an encryption using independent uniform coins, and let \(q_G\) bound classical queries to the key-and-coins hash. Then the stated oracle model gives
\[\Pr[\widehat K=K]\le\min\{1,q_G\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T_B)+2^{-256}\}.\]
A reduction guesses the first oracle query containing the hidden message. Before that query, the ciphertext distribution is exactly the native one with uniform coins. Full text gives the simulation, including why it need not know the coins or test which candidate message is correct.

This passive argument supplies no numerical hardness estimate and does not instantiate the stronger CCA theorem. In particular, average honest correctness is not automatically the message-wise correctness needed by a CCA reduction.

These inequalities are in the stated oracle model. A concrete-implementation claim must add the separate hash-transfer slack \(\delta_{\rm hash}\) and cap the result at one.

sections.title: Exact agreement first; a conditional tail later
sections.body:
The residual after cancellation is the truncated \(xr_2+r_1y+e\), whose weight is at most \(B=2ww_r+w_e\). A wrong repeated-RM symbol needs at least \(32r\) bit errors, conservatively including ties, and the outer RS decoder corrects \(\delta\) wrong symbols. Thus
\[B<(\delta+1)32r\]
guarantees every supported honest input decodes. Stages 1–4 satisfy this inequality and have unconditional zero mathematical disagreement.

For stages 5–66, the rational certificate establishes a ceiling \(2^{-128}\) only under the two displayed correctness premises. Full text separates the exact finite calculation from the unproved transfer to concrete seeded, correlated noise. Failure of the support inequality is not itself a decoding failure.

sections.title: Seed expansion does not worsen decoding
sections.body:
In \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), fix an encoder \(E:\{0,1\}^{128}\to\{0,1\}^L\), a decoder \(D:\{0,1\}^L\to\{0,1\}^{128}\cup\{\bot\}\), and coefficient truncation \(\pi_L\). Let \(F\) be the event \(D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\), with uniform message \(m\) and vector weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Compare two declared laws for these draws: \(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) uses the specified finite-seed hash expansions; \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) feeds independent uniform expansion streams into the same bounded samplers. The claim is \(\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm seed}}[F]\le\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}}[F]\). This is a one-sided failure-event claim, not equality of distributions; no additive error is silently omitted.

Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), truncation \(\pi_L\), and the specified repeated-RM/RS encoder and decoder \(E,D\). For a uniform 128-bit message and vectors with weights \(w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e\), define

\[
F(m,x,y,r_1,r_2,e)=\mathbf1\!\left[D\!\left(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e)\right)\ne m\right].
\]

This is the honest message-decoding failure event. Cancellation in the public equations gives exactly the displayed residual. Failure is averaged over honest messages and fresh keys; no supremum over maliciously chosen messages is taken. A retained decoder rejection is a failure. Native process crashes or invalid-generation operational errors are tracked separately, not discarded as successful observations.

\(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) is the actual finite-seed honest sampling law: it includes the public key seed, SHA3/SHAKE expansions, uniform message and salt, and the actual derivation of the encryption seed from those values. In particular it does not silently replace the concrete \(G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) encryption seed by a new independent draw. \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) replaces the declared honest expansion outputs by independent uniform expansion streams, consistently reused on repeated inputs, while retaining the same samplers, their bounds, the codec and its tie rules. The key sampler uses rejection for uniform fixed weight; the encryption sampler uses its specified fixed-work 32-bit procedure and retains that procedure's bias. No resampling is conditioned on successful decryption.

### Use in this construction

The binding is `hqc@modeled-research-v3`: 66 tuples from `crucible/data/hqc_model_profiles.json`, with \(n_1=16+2\delta\), \(1\le\delta\le15\), and \(1\le r\le3\). The fixed native source is liboqs commit `5a1a854b0dc9f2141bdc771c555ee60c37950183`, with the source/archive and specialization recorded in `docs/hqc-model-v3.txt`. Only the declared parameter headers are specialized. The construction, domain separators and seed maps retain the [2025-08-22 HQC specification](https://pqc-hqc.org/doc/hqc_specifications_2025_08_22.pdf), Sections 3.1–3.6. The 2026 specification is a different construction/parameter target and is not substituted for it.

The premise is needed only for the statistical correctness route at stages 5–66. Stages 1–4 have a separate deterministic support proof. `docs/hqc-model-v3.txt` fixes the ideal-expansion comparison and retained samplers; the authored full argument specifies the same honest failure event.

No transfer bound for the concrete expanders is proved. If evidence only supports \(\Pr_{\rm seed}[F]\le\Pr_{\rm ideal}[F]+\eta\), then \(\eta\) must remain in the final correctness bound. This premise concerns average decoding failure, not pseudorandomness against all distinguishers, the security hash transfer, or message-wise correctness required by stronger CCA arguments.

sections.title: Correlated noise obeys the decoder bound
sections.body:
Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), a repeated-RM/RS code \(E\), decoder \(D\), and the declared ideal-stream fixed-weight sampling law. For uniform 128-bit \(m\), put \(F=\{D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\}\). Let the explicit bound parameter \(B_{\rm model}\) be fixed by the full formula below: its coordinate parameter comes from uniform fixed supports, with finite RM error/tie bounds, RS correction radius, deterministic-tie correction and actual sampler-density factor all retained. The claim is \(\Pr[F]\le B_{\rm model}\). This compares one decoder event with an explicit bound; it does not claim that the residual coordinates are independent.

Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), truncation \(\pi_L\), and the specified repeated-RM/RS encoder and decoder \(E,D\). For a uniform 128-bit message and vectors with weights \(w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e\), define

\[
F(m,x,y,r_1,r_2,e)=\mathbf1\!\left[D\!\left(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e)\right)\ne m\right].
\]

This is the honest message-decoding failure event. Cancellation in the public equations gives exactly the displayed residual. Failure is averaged over honest messages and fresh keys; no supremum over maliciously chosen messages is taken. A retained decoder rejection is a failure. Native process crashes or invalid-generation operational errors are tracked separately, not discarded as successful observations.

\(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) is the actual finite-seed honest sampling law: it includes the public key seed, SHA3/SHAKE expansions, uniform message and salt, and the actual derivation of the encryption seed from those values. In particular it does not silently replace the concrete \(G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) encryption seed by a new independent draw. \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) replaces the declared honest expansion outputs by independent uniform expansion streams, consistently reused on repeated inputs, while retaining the same samplers, their bounds, the codec and its tie rules. The key sampler uses rejection for uniform fixed weight; the encryption sampler uses its specified fixed-work 32-bit procedure and retains that procedure's bias. No resampling is conditioned on successful decryption.

Here is the complete bound being claimed. Let \(n_1=16+2\delta\), repetition \(r\), and

\[
a=\sum_{\substack{j\text{ odd}}}\frac{\binom wj\binom{n-w}{w_r-j}}{\binom n{w_r}},\qquad
p=2a(1-a)(1-w_e/n)+(a^2+(1-a)^2)w_e/n.
\]

This \(p\) is the one-coordinate marginal for independent uniform fixed supports. It alone does not determine the tail of the correlated residual. The surrogate substitutes independent Bernoulli coordinates. For a repeated RM block let \(d=64r\), and take binomial coefficients outside their valid range to be zero. Define the finite weight counts

\[
b_i=\min\!\left\{2\binom{2d}i,\ 255\binom d{d/2}\binom d{i-d/2}
+510\sum_{j=d/2+1}^{d}\binom dj\binom d{i-j}
+\binom{255}{2}\sum_{j=0}^{d/2}\binom{d/2}j^3\binom{d/2}{i-d+j}\right\}.
\]

The inner error majorant and tie majorant are

\[
\pi=\frac12\sum_{i=0}^{2d}b_i p^i(1-p)^{2d-i},\qquad
\tau=\min\!\left\{1,255\binom d{d/2}[p(1-p)]^{d/2}\right\}.
\]

With \(\beta=(1+n/2^{32})^{2w_r+w_e}\), the complete outer expression is

\[
B_{\rm model}=\min\!\left\{1,\beta\left[\sum_{j=\delta+1}^{n_1}\binom{n_1}j\pi^j(1-\pi)^{n_1-j}
+\binom{n_1}{17}\tau^{17}\right]\right\}.
\]

The retained calculation rounds \(p\) upward to a 64-bit dyadic grid after checking the finite majorant's monotonicity, then rounds \(\pi,\tau\) upward to 256-bit dyadics. The rest is exact rational arithmetic. These conservative values, not unrounded floating approximations, define the bound in the premise. The final term handles the stated deterministic-tie coupling for uniform 16-byte RS messages; \(\beta\) retains the fixed-work encapsulation sampler's density adjustment.

### Use in this construction

The binding is `hqc@modeled-research-v3`: 66 tuples from `crucible/data/hqc_model_profiles.json`, with \(n_1=16+2\delta\), \(1\le\delta\le15\), and \(1\le r\le3\). The fixed native source is liboqs commit `5a1a854b0dc9f2141bdc771c555ee60c37950183`, with the source/archive and specialization recorded in `docs/hqc-model-v3.txt`. Only the declared parameter headers are specialized. The construction, domain separators and seed maps retain the [2025-08-22 HQC specification](https://pqc-hqc.org/doc/hqc_specifications_2025_08_22.pdf), Sections 3.1–3.6. The 2026 specification is a different construction/parameter target and is not substituted for it.

The premise applies to the statistical route at stages 5–66. The complete arithmetic is executable in `crucible/hqc_model_correctness.py` and pinned by each profile's certificate. It proves \(B_{\rm model}\le2^{-128}\) for those selected tuples; it does not prove the comparison \(\Pr[F]\le B_{\rm model}\).

The bound's provenance is the [2026-10-12 HQC specification](https://pqc-hqc.org/doc/hqc_specifications_2026_10_12.pdf), Sections 6.1.1–6.1.5 and 6.2.3, retaining Model 1 and the declared tie and bias corrections for this older construction. Its use on reduced tuples is an explicit unproved transfer. Actual cyclic products have correlations and fixed parity; equal marginals are insufficient, and ordinary simulation cannot certify a \(2^{-128}\) tail. A counterexample to independence alone would not refute this weaker event bound.

sections.title: The earlier reference and remaining cryptanalysis
sections.body:
The earlier catalogue supplied no calibrated attack-cost curve for these 66 tuples. The elementary bit-RAM attacks below now provide explicit conditional work bounds. Competitive best-known attack estimates still require further cryptanalysis.

The October 2026 specification changes weights and other construction details. The retained August 2025 release cannot inherit the newer assessment, and conditional correctness is not a confidentiality estimate. An alternative low-weight solution to one public equation need not yield the target key; each attack must include its actual success argument and final key derivation.

sections.title: Seeded noisy-product message recovery
sections.body:
Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), an injective 128-bit message code \(E\) of length \(L\le n\), and public seed maps \(S_K,H_X,S_R\). From independent uniform 256-bit seeds obtain \((\alpha,x,y)=S_K(\sigma)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\), with weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Draw \(m\) uniformly from 128 bits. Publish \(\alpha,s=x+hy,u=r_1+hr_2,v=E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e)\), where \(\pi_L\) truncates to \(L\) coefficients. The claim is \(\Pr[A(\alpha,s,u,v)=m]\le\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T)\) for every classical algorithm of bit-RAM work at most \(T\). The seed maps and claimed success bound are parameters, not implicit uniformity or security guarantees.

The public parameters are \((n,w,w_r,w_e,n_1,r)\), the code \(E:\{0,1\}^{128}\to\{0,1\}^{L}\) with \(L=128rn_1\le n\), its decoder \(D\), and specified deterministic seed maps. In \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), addition is coefficientwise XOR and multiplication is cyclic convolution. The map \(\pi_L\) keeps the first \(L\) coefficients.

\(S_K\) maps a uniform 256-bit initial key seed to a public seed \(\alpha\) and secret vectors \(x,y\), both of weight \(w\), using the specified key-generation expansion and successful-generation rules. \(H_X(\alpha)=h\) is the public vector expansion. \(S_R(\theta)=(r_1,r_2,e)\) expands a 256-bit encryption seed, with weights \((w_r,w_r,w_e)\). These maps, including finite-seed correlations, rejection rules and sampling bias, are public parameters of the problem. They are not assumed to produce uniform independent ring elements.

The public key is \(P=(\alpha,s)\), where \(s=x+hy\). Define the core encryption map

\[
\mathcal E(P,m;\theta)=\left(r_1+hr_2,\ E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e)\right),\qquad (r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta).
\]

The public seed \(\alpha\), not merely its expansion \(h\), is included in the attacker's input. The retained codec is an outer RS\((n_1,16)\) code over \(\mathbb F_{256}\), followed by \(r\)-fold repeated RM\((1,7)\); its field representation, coordinate order and deterministic tie rules are part of \(E,D\).

The message and both initial seeds are independent. Winning means returning the actual 128-bit message, with probability over those draws and the attacker's coins. The work budget counts all attacker preprocessing and verification. This formulation includes attacks exploiting the public seed, code, truncation, parity, ring structure or concrete expanders.

### Use in this construction

The binding is `hqc@modeled-research-v3`: 66 tuples from `crucible/data/hqc_model_profiles.json`, with \(n_1=16+2\delta\), \(1\le\delta\le15\), and \(1\le r\le3\). The fixed native source is liboqs commit `5a1a854b0dc9f2141bdc771c555ee60c37950183`, with the source/archive and specialization recorded in `docs/hqc-model-v3.txt`. Only the declared parameter headers are specialized. The construction, domain separators and seed maps retain the [2025-08-22 HQC specification](https://pqc-hqc.org/doc/hqc_specifications_2025_08_22.pdf), Sections 3.1–3.6. The 2026 specification is a different construction/parameter target and is not substituted for it.

This is the exact core one-wayness premise used by the local passive key-recovery proof. The 2025 specification's Theorem 6.2 offers a different, distinguishing route through parity-aware 2-DQCSD and truncated 3-DQCSD. No reduction from this particular finite-seed, reduced-parameter message-recovery problem to those idealized problems is supplied here. Calling it simply “syndrome decoding is hard” would hide that missing bridge. No numerical \(\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T)\), CCA guarantee or asymptotic negligible bound is inferred.

sections.title: Key-and-coins hash transfer
sections.body:
Fix the ring encryption map \(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta)=(r_1+hr_2,E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e))\), where \(P=(\alpha,s=x+hy)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\). Generate \(P\) by the declared key seed map; draw independent uniform 128-bit \(m,z\). Set \((K,\theta)=G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) and \(C=(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta),z)\). Let \(p_{\rm real}(T,Q)\) be the best classical probability of recovering \(K\) from \((P,C)\) with work \(T\) and \(Q\) calls to domain-separated SHA3-512 role \(G\). Define \(p_{\rm ideal}\) with only \(G\) replaced by an independent random function to 512 bits. The claim is \(p_{\rm real}\le p_{\rm ideal}+\delta_{\rm hash}(T,Q)\); no small slack is proved.

The public parameters are \((n,w,w_r,w_e,n_1,r)\), the code \(E:\{0,1\}^{128}\to\{0,1\}^{L}\) with \(L=128rn_1\le n\), its decoder \(D\), and specified deterministic seed maps. In \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), addition is coefficientwise XOR and multiplication is cyclic convolution. The map \(\pi_L\) keeps the first \(L\) coefficients.

\(S_K\) maps a uniform 256-bit initial key seed to a public seed \(\alpha\) and secret vectors \(x,y\), both of weight \(w\), using the specified key-generation expansion and successful-generation rules. \(H_X(\alpha)=h\) is the public vector expansion. \(S_R(\theta)=(r_1,r_2,e)\) expands a 256-bit encryption seed, with weights \((w_r,w_r,w_e)\). These maps, including finite-seed correlations, rejection rules and sampling bias, are public parameters of the problem. They are not assumed to produce uniform independent ring elements.

The public key is \(P=(\alpha,s)\), where \(s=x+hy\). Define the core encryption map

\[
\mathcal E(P,m;\theta)=\left(r_1+hr_2,\ E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e)\right),\qquad (r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta).
\]

The public seed \(\alpha\), not merely its expansion \(h\), is included in the attacker's input. The retained codec is an outer RS\((n_1,16)\) code over \(\mathbb F_{256}\), followed by \(r\)-fold repeated RM\((1,7)\); its field representation, coordinate order and deterministic tie rules are part of \(E,D\).

\(H(P)\) is the concrete, domain-separated SHA3-256 public-key digest. The independent public salt \(z\) is 16 bytes; \(G\)'s first and second 32-byte halves are \(K\) and \(\theta\). A designated random-function response is sampled once for each new input and reused on repeats. Only \(G\) changes between the two experiments; \(H\), the other hash roles and all seed maps remain concrete. All pre-challenge \(G\) calls count toward \(Q\).

This is a bounded comparison of complete-key recovery, not a claim that fixed SHA3 code is indistinguishable from an independent random function for arbitrary tests. It makes no collision-resistance premise about \(H\) in this single-public-key experiment.

Here “best” is a supremum over the declared uniform classical bit-RAM algorithm class, including its work and query limits. The real and ideal suprema may be attained or approached by different algorithms. This is not the stronger claim that each individual program has the same real/ideal success. The model comparison must use compatible conventions for preprocessing, available public information and hash-call accounting.

### Use in this construction

The binding is `hqc@modeled-research-v3`: 66 tuples from `crucible/data/hqc_model_profiles.json`, with \(n_1=16+2\delta\), \(1\le\delta\le15\), and \(1\le r\le3\). The fixed native source is liboqs commit `5a1a854b0dc9f2141bdc771c555ee60c37950183`, with the source/archive and specialization recorded in `docs/hqc-model-v3.txt`. Only the declared parameter headers are specialized. The construction, domain separators and seed maps retain the [2025-08-22 HQC specification](https://pqc-hqc.org/doc/hqc_specifications_2025_08_22.pdf), Sections 3.1–3.6. The 2026 specification is a different construction/parameter target and is not substituted for it.

The local first-target-query argument yields the ideal passive bound \(\min\{1,Q\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T_B)+2^{-256}\}\). The concrete conclusion must add \(\delta_{\rm hash}(T,Q)\), capped at one. \(T_B\) charges simulation and all other computation; the factor \(Q\) is retained. This model premise is distinct from both correctness premises: it does not say that cyclic-product noise is independent, does not prove decoder correctness, and does not extend the passive argument to full CCA or quantum security.

sections.title: One common measure of attack work
sections.body:
These curves use **Classical bit-RAM v1**: elementary Boolean operations and one-bit memory transfers share a fixed accounting rule. All attack setup is charged to one fresh challenge. Memory capacity is unlimited in this abstraction, and the storage bound remains visible beside the graph.

The plotted quantity is \(\log_2 W\), where \(W\) bounds a specified strategy's work and its stated assumptions imply at least **50% probability of recovering the complete shared key**. These are reproducible **baseline upper bounds**, not the cheapest known attacks or a security lower bound. A bigger value does not establish a more secure scheme. Full text contains the cost rules, proofs, parameter table and reproduction commands.

sections.title: Searching the private support
sections.body: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.

sections.title: An information-set attack on the private key
sections.body: Recover the small private vector from the public relation s=x+hy, then decode the ciphertext and derive its 32-byte secret. The displayed budget uses the cheaper of full support enumeration and a simple information-set attack, with the relevant assumptions shown for that choice. It includes decoding and hashing. This baseline omits faster specialized attacks and is not estimated best-known security.

sections.title: A-32 · Almost every public key has a unique small secret
sections.body:
Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.

Applies to Stages 1–66.

sections.title: A-33 · Enough information sets remain invertible
sections.body:
For at least seven eighths of honest targets, at least one eighth of the selected column sets that contain the true error support give an invertible matrix. This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.

Applies to Stages 4–66.

sections.title: A-34 · The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
sections.body:
The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.

Applies to Stages 5–66.

assumptions.label: A-1
assumptions.statement: In \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), fix an encoder \(E:\{0,1\}^{128}\to\{0,1\}^L\), a decoder \(D:\{0,1\}^L\to\{0,1\}^{128}\cup\{\bot\}\), and coefficient truncation \(\pi_L\). Let \(F\) be the event \(D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\), with uniform message \(m\) and vector weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Compare two declared laws for these draws: \(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) uses the specified finite-seed hash expansions; \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) feeds independent uniform expansion streams into the same bounded samplers. The claim is \(\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm seed}}[F]\le\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}}[F]\). This is a one-sided failure-event claim, not equality of distributions; no additive error is silently omitted.
assumptions.scope: Stages 5–66 along the conditional correctness route; no additive error is filled in.
assumptions.summary: Replacing ideal randomness by the specified finite-seed expanders does not increase the probability of honest decoding failure.

assumptions.label: A-2
assumptions.statement:
Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), a repeated-RM/RS code \(E\), decoder \(D\), and the declared ideal-stream fixed-weight sampling law. For uniform 128-bit \(m\), put \(F=\{D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\}\). Let the explicit bound parameter \(B_{\rm model}\) be fixed by the full formula below: its coordinate parameter comes from uniform fixed supports, with finite RM error/tie bounds, RS correction radius, deterministic-tie correction and actual sampler-density factor all retained. The claim is \(\Pr[F]\le B_{\rm model}\). This compares one decoder event with an explicit bound; it does not claim that the residual coordinates are independent.

Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), truncation \(\pi_L\), and the specified repeated-RM/RS encoder and decoder \(E,D\). For a uniform 128-bit message and vectors with weights \(w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e\), define

\[
F(m,x,y,r_1,r_2,e)=\mathbf1\!\left[D\!\left(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e)\right)\ne m\right].
\]

This is the honest message-decoding failure event. Cancellation in the public equations gives exactly the displayed residual. Failure is averaged over honest messages and fresh keys; no supremum over maliciously chosen messages is taken. A retained decoder rejection is a failure. Native process crashes or invalid-generation operational errors are tracked separately, not discarded as successful observations.

\(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) is the actual finite-seed honest sampling law: it includes the public key seed, SHA3/SHAKE expansions, uniform message and salt, and the actual derivation of the encryption seed from those values. In particular it does not silently replace the concrete \(G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) encryption seed by a new independent draw. \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) replaces the declared honest expansion outputs by independent uniform expansion streams, consistently reused on repeated inputs, while retaining the same samplers, their bounds, the codec and its tie rules. The key sampler uses rejection for uniform fixed weight; the encryption sampler uses its specified fixed-work 32-bit procedure and retains that procedure's bias. No resampling is conditioned on successful decryption.

Here is the complete bound being claimed. Let \(n_1=16+2\delta\), repetition \(r\), and

\[
a=\sum_{\substack{j\text{ odd}}}\frac{\binom wj\binom{n-w}{w_r-j}}{\binom n{w_r}},\qquad
p=2a(1-a)(1-w_e/n)+(a^2+(1-a)^2)w_e/n.
\]

This \(p\) is the one-coordinate marginal for independent uniform fixed supports. It alone does not determine the tail of the correlated residual. The surrogate substitutes independent Bernoulli coordinates. For a repeated RM block let \(d=64r\), and take binomial coefficients outside their valid range to be zero. Define the finite weight counts

\[
b_i=\min\!\left\{2\binom{2d}i,\ 255\binom d{d/2}\binom d{i-d/2}
+510\sum_{j=d/2+1}^{d}\binom dj\binom d{i-j}
+\binom{255}{2}\sum_{j=0}^{d/2}\binom{d/2}j^3\binom{d/2}{i-d+j}\right\}.
\]

The inner error majorant and tie majorant are

\[
\pi=\frac12\sum_{i=0}^{2d}b_i p^i(1-p)^{2d-i},\qquad
\tau=\min\!\left\{1,255\binom d{d/2}[p(1-p)]^{d/2}\right\}.
\]

With \(\beta=(1+n/2^{32})^{2w_r+w_e}\), the complete outer expression is

\[
B_{\rm model}=\min\!\left\{1,\beta\left[\sum_{j=\delta+1}^{n_1}\binom{n_1}j\pi^j(1-\pi)^{n_1-j}
+\binom{n_1}{17}\tau^{17}\right]\right\}.
\]

The retained calculation rounds \(p\) upward to a 64-bit dyadic grid after checking the finite majorant's monotonicity, then rounds \(\pi,\tau\) upward to 256-bit dyadics. The rest is exact rational arithmetic. These conservative values, not unrounded floating approximations, define the bound in the premise. The final term handles the stated deterministic-tie coupling for uniform 16-byte RS messages; \(\beta\) retains the fixed-work encapsulation sampler's density adjustment.
assumptions.scope: Stages 5–66; exact ring, supports, truncation, codec and message experiment.
assumptions.summary: The stated conservative calculation bounds decoder failure despite correlations in the actual cyclic-product noise.

assumptions.label: A-27
assumptions.statement: Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), an injective 128-bit message code \(E\) of length \(L\le n\), and public seed maps \(S_K,H_X,S_R\). From independent uniform 256-bit seeds obtain \((\alpha,x,y)=S_K(\sigma)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\), with weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Draw \(m\) uniformly from 128 bits. Publish \(\alpha,s=x+hy,u=r_1+hr_2,v=E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e)\), where \(\pi_L\) truncates to \(L\) coefficients. The claim is \(\Pr[A(\alpha,s,u,v)=m]\le\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T)\) for every classical algorithm of bit-RAM work at most \(T\). The seed maps and claimed success bound are parameters, not implicit uniformity or security guarantees.
assumptions.scope: All66 current tuples. The core uses the actual finite-seed expansions and biased sampler; no uniform-matrix or ideal-IID transfer is silently substituted.
assumptions.summary: A message remains hard to recover from two noisy products in a binary polynomial ring.

assumptions.label: A-28
assumptions.statement: Fix the ring encryption map \(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta)=(r_1+hr_2,E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e))\), where \(P=(\alpha,s=x+hy)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\). Generate \(P\) by the declared key seed map; draw independent uniform 128-bit \(m,z\). Set \((K,\theta)=G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) and \(C=(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta),z)\). Let \(p_{\rm real}(T,Q)\) be the best classical probability of recovering \(K\) from \((P,C)\) with work \(T\) and \(Q\) calls to domain-separated SHA3-512 role \(G\). Define \(p_{\rm ideal}\) with only \(G\) replaced by an independent random function to 512 bits. The claim is \(p_{\rm real}\le p_{\rm ideal}+\delta_{\rm hash}(T,Q)\); no small slack is proved.
assumptions.scope: All exact registered profiles in this note. The oracle theorem is exact in its model; transferring it to the concrete hash roles is a separate unproved premise, not a claim that a fixed public function literally behaves randomly.
assumptions.summary: Deriving the key and encryption seed with the concrete hash preserves the ideal experiment’s recovery bound, up to an explicit slack.

hqc@modeled-research-v3.full_text_appendix:
## Reproducible bit-RAM attack analysis

## Shared computation model: crucible-bit-ram-v1

The program is uniform in public configuration inputs; no answer-dependent
advice is permitted. Its fixed-address bit registers support arbitrary Boolean
functions of one or two bits at unit cost. Constants, fixed wiring and fixed bit
permutations are free. A dynamically addressed bit read or write costs one;
computing that address is additional charged arithmetic. This is a bit-RAM
abstraction inspired by NIST's classical gate-count discussions, not the CAT
pure circuit metric and not a NIST-approved scheme classification.

The baseline has no memory-cap constraint. It measures neither physical latency
nor energy. A pointer of b bits must be manipulated with the b-bit arithmetic
account. Loops use a public counter width and charge increment/comparison.
Input generation for the honest challenger is outside the attack budget; all
attacker initialization, candidate generation, verification and key derivation
are inside. Randomness and any rejection sampling need explicit budgets or
their own success-loss treatment. A counter on high-level Python operations is
validation of the operation census, not a trace of exact elementary gates.

Primitive upper bounds, for width w: ADD/SUB/CMP=8w; MUX=3w;
MODADD=24(w+1); MUL=16(w+1)^2; DIVMOD=64(w+1)^2;
MODMUL=80(w+1)^2; LOOP(b)=16(b+1).
MODPOW(w,e)=e(2 MODMUL(w)+MUX(w)+LOOP(e))+2w.
All bounds refer to schoolbook/ripple, restoring-division and double-and-add
algorithms. They deliberately upper-bound a particular implementation.

SHA-256/SHA-512 follow FIPS180-4. The schedule uses two small sigmas and three
word additions per expanded word. Each round uses two large sigmas, Ch, Maj,
and seven additions. Eight final additions update the chaining value. Padding
and block input/output are charged. SHA3/SHAKE follow FIPS202: Keccak-f[1600]
uses at most193536 Boolean operations (24 rounds of8064), padded to200000
for control. Absorption and output transfers are additional. These are
algorithmic upper bounds, not claims about optimized hardware.

Every profile's complete attack is stopped within its reported budget. Its
success statement names the probability space and any unproved premises.
The resulting curve is a documented attack upper bound, not a proven security
level and not necessarily the cheapest known attack. No 50%-success result is
inferred simply by dividing cost by average success probability.

Primary specifications:
- https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.180-4.pdf
- https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.202.pdf


## Reproduction

From this source checkout:
```text
python scripts/build_ram_attack_notes.py --check
python -m pytest tests/test_ram_common.py tests/test_ram_classical_attacks.py tests/test_ram_lattice_attacks.py tests/test_ram_code_attacks.py tests/test_ram_catalogue.py
```
The generated `crucible/data/ram_attack_curves.json` retains integer cost components, parameters, assumptions and source-file hashes. No cryptographic-size attack is executed. Small examples check implementation paths; they do not verify heuristic premises at large sizes. No external model service or paid API is used.

## Searching the private support

Worked configuration: hqc-modeled-research-v3-tier-3. The same algorithm and parameterized formulas generate the other rows below.

## Attack specification: private support recovery then full KEM completion

The retained HQC2025 public relation is s=x+h*y in F2[X]/(X^n-1), where
wt(x)=wt(y)=w. One baseline enumerates every weight-w y, forms x=s+h*y,
and accepts when wt(x)=w. Another applies the explicitly bounded Prange
algorithm to H=[I_n|rot(h)], N=2n, r=n and target weight2w, then checks the
individual half weights. The smaller documented work budget is selected;
its premise set is selected with it. Prange uses the same rank-density
hypothesis and R=ceil(32 binom(2n,2w)/binom(n,2w)) accounting as the McEliece
note. Exhaustive enumeration needs no rank hypothesis and no uniform-secret
assumption: the true support is always visited.

For motivation, first analyze an ideal independent uniform public multiplier.
In that auxiliary model another weight-(w,w) solution has probability at most
epsilon=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)/2^(n-1). To see this, for y'!=y,
y+y' has even parity. Since n is primitive prime and2w<n-1, this nonzero
polynomial is not divisible by the irreducible degree-(n-1) factor of X^n-1.
Multiplication by it maps uniform h uniformly onto the even-parity subspace.
Each fixed x' therefore satisfies the alternative equation with probability
at most2^-(n-1). Apply a union bound; no independence of those alternatives
is needed. The bound is checked per profile and is below1/64. For the actual
fixed SHAKE implementation the visible premise is only that alternative-key
probability is at most1/64. This is an unproved event-level transfer claim;
the tiny ideal-model bound is not transplanted to the finite seeded output
space. The attack explicitly computes SHAKE and pays its cost.

Once y is recovered, compute v+u*y and truncate to the code length. For each
repeated RM(1,7) block, compare all256 affine words and choose nearest,
breaking ties by linear-mask order and then the constant bit. Decode the
shortened cyclic RS code using syndromes, Berlekamp-Massey, locator roots and
a GF256 Vandermonde solve for error values; recheck syndromes. Extract the
systematic16-byte message. The full secret is the first32 bytes of
SHA3-512(SHA3-256(pk||0x01)||message||salt||0x00).

The primitive-recovery success is at least1-1/64 for full support enumeration,
or at least21/32-1/64 for Prange. The existing October29 support proof bounds
the honest residual weight by B=2*w*wr+we. A repeated RM block can decode
incorrectly only after at least32*r errors, counting ties as potentially wrong;
RS(16+2*delta,16) corrects delta wrong symbols. Thus B<(delta+1)*32*r proves
zero honest decoding failure for every supported draw, without an ideal-XOF
or independent-noise premise. The actual tuple is checked against this strict
criterion; among the current66 profiles exactly stages1-4 satisfy it. See
docs/hqc-module-progression-review-20261029.txt and
docs/hqc-support-review-20261029.json. Otherwise subtract the actual honest
decoding-failure probability<=2^-128 using the explicit conditional premise.
No independence between correctness, rank and uniqueness events is assumed.

The budget charges SHAKE expansion, public-matrix construction (Prange only),
all finite trials/support candidates, cyclic multiplication, an explicit256-word
nearest-RM decoder, polynomial RS decoding and both final SHA3 evaluations.
GF256 multiplication uses eight shift/XOR/reduction rounds (<=1024 bit ops),
and inversion by x^254 costs<=16 multiplications. RS work is bounded by
4L^3+32L^2+512L+4096 field/control slots, each paying1024 plus the address/
transfer/control allowance; this covers the cubic error-value solve, all
syndrome evaluations, BM, root evaluation and initialization. The reference
Python kernel executes this path but its wall-clock runtime is not the unit.
The implementation deliberately overcounts rather than claiming optimized
native timings. Source parameters and byte formats are those of the exact
modeled-research-v3 adapter; the2026 HQC parameter changes are not imported.

These baselines do not represent the cheapest known HQC attacks. In particular,
quasi-cyclic improvements, modern ISD and public-message enumeration may be
cheaper. The conditional upper-bound curve should not be labelled a lower
bound on security or evidence that a NIST category is met.

For this tuple B=2*w*wr+we=28 < (delta+1)*32*r=64. The existing support proof therefore gives zero honest decoding failure, including deterministic ties, without an independent-noise or ideal-XOF premise. No correctness failure term is subtracted.


Success statement for this worked configuration: 1 - 1/64 > 1/2

## A-32 · Almost every public key has a unique small secret

The required concrete premise is Pr_actual[there exists another weight-(w,w) pair x',y' with s=x'+h*y']<=1/64. Thus the ideal failure probability is <=binom(n,w)(binom(n,w)-1)2^-(n-1). This much smaller ideal bound is supporting rationale only. We do not assert a fixed SHAKE image of 256-bit seeds is literally uniform over n bits or transfer that tiny ideal bound without justification. The attack computes actual SHAKE and subtracts1/64, not the ideal-model probability, in its success claim.

## A-33 · Enough information sets remain invertible

Write H as an r-by-N binary matrix and e for the actual weight-t target. With probability at least7/8 over the honest target draw, Pr_J[rank(H_J)=r | supp(e) subset J] >=1/8, where J is uniform among r-subsets. This is a per-instance density condition on a 7/8-measure good set, not an average success probability that can be amplified without justification. Fresh trials are independent conditional on H,e. Neither random-matrix heuristics nor toy checks prove this claim for binary Goppa or quasi-cyclic matrices.

## A-34 · The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme

Use the retained per-profile conditional correctness certificate and its model-transfer premise to assert Pr[the concatenated nearest-RM/bounded-distance-RS decoder fails on an honest encapsulation]<=2^-128. The explicit attack decoder uses the same nearest-RM tie order (linear mask first, then constant) and the unique RS codeword within delta symbol errors. This transfer includes compatibility of those tie and decoding conventions. Subtract this failure probability by union bound; independence from rank or uniqueness events is not assumed.

hqc@modeled-research-v3.full_text_argument_appendix:
## Exact security and correctness argument: HQC modeled research v3

### A narrow security statement for the actual retained transform

Fix one exact current tuple. The native PKE core retains its actual SHAKE seed expansion, fixed-weight samplers, finite ring, RS/RM code, truncation and key-generation process. Define the core one-way game as follows: generate a native key pair; choose m uniformly from 128 bits and theta independently uniformly from 256 bits; give (pk,Encrypt(pk,m;theta)) to B; B wins if it returns m. Let OW_PKE(T) bound the best classical success probability at budget T. This definition incorporates all finite-seed and sampler effects. It does not claim that the actual core already has a reduction to uniformly sampled DQCSD.

The 2025 transform computes a=H(pk), samples a public uniform 128-bit salt s, and sets

    (K,theta)=G(a||m||s),   C=(Encrypt(pk,m;theta),s).

G is the domain-separated SHA3-512 role, split into two 256-bit halves; H is the specified SHA3-256 public-key digest. For this theorem G is an independent random oracle, separate from H/I/J and the PKE expansion algorithms. There is no need to make H collision-free in a single fixed-public-key experiment: the target query is defined by its actual a bytes. Queries made through another public key with the same digest still count as queries to that same input. Fixed field lengths make the message and salt parsing unambiguous.

The attacker receives one honest C and pk and returns the entire 256-bit K. It has no decapsulation or answer-checking oracle. Let q_G be an upper bound on its distinct G queries; all public arithmetic and other hash evaluations are included in its work budget.

### First-target-query reduction, including the hidden coins

In a lazy-table experiment, the KEM's G entry at x*=a||m||s has independent uniform output (K,theta). Until A first queries x*, the challenge ciphertext is distributed as an ordinary core encryption with independent uniform theta, and K is a hidden independent uniform half. A has no access to this programmed entry before that query. This remains true if oracle precomputation is allowed: a target query during precomputation is itself the first target event and is counted.

Reduction B receives a core challenge (pk,c) with hidden m and hidden independent coins theta. It chooses and privately holds a uniform salt s before any allowed pre-challenge computation. It gives pk to A and answers pre-challenge G queries using the same lazy table; it withholds C=(c,s) until the challenge phase. The preselected salt remains hidden until then. Post-challenge queries use that same table. At the start it chooses J uniformly from {1,...,q_G}. When the J-th distinct query has the target public-digest and salt framing, it outputs the message component of that query and stops; otherwise it fails. It need not recognize the true query, invert theta, or re-encrypt a candidate. Runs with fewer than J queries fail.

For every j, if the first target query is j, the real and simulated views before that query have the same distribution: all earlier table entries are independent of the challenge, while the challenge coins are uniform in both games. If J=j, B stops before returning the inconsistent arbitrary answer at that first target query. Summing over j gives

    Pr[Ask x* in the real game] <= q_G * Pr[B recovers m].

There is no claim that the entire simulation stays correct after a missed target query. It need not: the reduction only uses the runs whose guessed index is the first such query. Without Ask x*, K remains an unobserved independent 256-bit value, so one final guess succeeds with probability 2^-256. Therefore

    Pr[A recovers K] <= min(1,q_G*OW_PKE(T_B)+2^-256).

For q_G=0 the key-guess term is the whole bound. T_B consists of A, the public digest/salt handling and lazy-table simulation; no unspecified decoder oracle is used. If an adversary can decrypt some messages ambiguously, that affects the core one-way success function; the reduction never assumes perfect PKE correctness. This theorem is a manually checked local derivation for passive classical key recovery. It is not a concrete numerical lower bound, a QROM proof, or a full IND-CCA application.

The 2025 specification's Theorem 6.2 gives an idealized PKE distinguishing route via 2-DQCSD-P and truncated parity-aware 3-DQCSD-PT. Its Theorem 6.3 additionally uses a stronger message-wise delta-correctness condition for the salted CCA transform. Our average honest-failure certificate does not silently discharge that condition, and the current native-key distribution is not replaced by a uniformly random matrix. Those stronger applications remain outside this theorem rather than being hidden as proof assumptions.

### Honest cancellation and the deterministic region

With s=x+hy, u=r1+hr2 and v=Encode(m)+s*r2+e, decryption cancels h*y*r2 and leaves Encode(m)+x*r2+r1*y+e on the transmitted code coordinates. A cyclic binary product has weight at most the product of the input weights; cancellation and truncation can only reduce this upper bound. Hence the residual weight is at most B=2*w*wr+we, for every allowed support draw, independently of its distribution.

A repeated RM(1,7) inner code has minimum distance 64*r. Fewer than 32*r errors in a block force the transmitted inner word to be the unique nearest word. Counting a tie as potentially bad, each bad block consumes at least 32*r errors. If B<(delta+1)*32*r, at most delta blocks can be bad, and the outer RS code's distance 2*delta+1 corrects them. The native decoder's documented nearest-RM and bounded-distance RS algorithms therefore recover m. Re-encryption with the same deterministic G output matches C and returns the identical K, regardless of hash idealization.

The exact frozen table gives first-four residual bounds 6,15,28,45 with guaranteed overall capacity 63; stage 5 has bound 66. Thus the support proof gives zero disagreement at stages 1–4. It does not claim failure at stage 5 or later. No independence, random-oracle or hardness assumption is needed for that support proof; it concerns the mathematical algorithms under valid successful generation, not a formal proof of the C implementation.

### The statistical region and its two separate premises

For stages 5–66, set E_actual=the concrete seeded honest-decoding-failure event. The finite-expansion premise is a one-sided comparison Pr[E_actual]<=Pr[E_ideal] for the named ideal expansion experiment. The decoder-event premise bounds Pr[E_ideal] by the full adjusted surrogate expression B_model below. Neither is obtained by treating correlated cyclic-product bits as literally independent. If a justified transfer instead has additive epsilon, the final bound is B_model+epsilon, not B_model.

For independent uniform supports, let a=sum_{j odd} C(w,j)C(n-w,wr-j)/C(n,wr) be the odd-overlap probability for one cyclic product coordinate. The exact one-coordinate residual marginal is

    p=2*a*(1-a)*(1-we/n)+(a*a+(1-a)*(1-a))*we/n.

Inside the surrogate, coordinates are independent Bernoulli(p). The retained calculator obtains an RM error bound pi and tie bound tau using the code's exact finite weight counts, including two-way and multiway ties; it then uses

    B_model = min(1, beta * [sum_{j=delta+1}^{n1} C(n1,j)pi^j(1-pi)^(n1-j)
                            + C(n1,17)*tau^17]),
    beta=(1+n/2^32)^(2*wr+we).

The second term retains the specified deterministic-tie coupling correction for a uniform 16-byte RS message. beta is the conservative density adjustment for the actual fixed-work encapsulation sampler. p is rounded upward to a 64-bit dyadic grid; pi and tau are rounded upward to 256-bit dyadics after checking the finite majorant's monotonicity. Remaining arithmetic and comparison to 2^-128 use exact integers/rationals. The source and certificate pins identify all these choices. The arithmetic proves B_model<=2^-128 for the selected tuples, not either transfer premise and not a worst-message CCA correctness bound.

### Evidence and reproduction

The construction and G/H framing are in the HQC 2025 specification Sections 3.1,3.5–3.6; its Section 6.2 distinguishes the PKE/CCA proof games. Correctness-model provenance is recorded in docs/hqc-model-v3.txt and the 2026 specification Sections 6.1.1–6.1.5. This note's passive first-query theorem is authored here, not copied as an upstream theorem.

Run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_hqc_model.py -k 'every_tier_exact_sizes_and_unconditioned_honest_agreement or frozen_parameter_certificates'` for the 66 exact current tuples and certificate replay; run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_hqc_support_review.py` for scope/boundary tests. `crucible/hqc_model_correctness.py` exposes the exact arithmetic. Native samples do not establish rare-event probabilities or computational hardness.

### Transfer to concrete hashing

The inequalities above are mathematical claims in the specified ideal experiment. For the concrete hash roles, the separate premise bounds the concrete key-recovery probability by that ideal probability plus delta_hash(T,Q), for the explicitly declared algorithm and resource class. Add this term to the right side and cap at one. No small numerical value of delta_hash is proved here. This is an operational, construction-specific transfer premise; it does not assert that an adversary cannot distinguish a publicly computable fixed SHA function from a freshly sampled oracle by directly comparing their outputs. A generic collision-resistance statement would not justify the transfer.

Reproduce the finite parameter/coefficient/code checks with `python scripts/check_scheme_code_arguments.py`. The validation receipt `docs/evidence/scheme-code-arguments-20261105.json` records the current native checks and the two missing-fixture limitations explicitly.

statements.label: A-1
statements.title: Seed expansion does not worsen decoding
statements.definition: In \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), fix an encoder \(E:\{0,1\}^{128}\to\{0,1\}^L\), a decoder \(D:\{0,1\}^L\to\{0,1\}^{128}\cup\{\bot\}\), and coefficient truncation \(\pi_L\). Let \(F\) be the event \(D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\), with uniform message \(m\) and vector weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Compare two declared laws for these draws: \(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) uses the specified finite-seed hash expansions; \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) feeds independent uniform expansion streams into the same bounded samplers. The claim is \(\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm seed}}[F]\le\Pr_{\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}}[F]\). This is a one-sided failure-event claim, not equality of distributions; no additive error is silently omitted.

statements.label: A-2
statements.title: Correlated noise obeys the decoder bound
statements.definition:
Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), a repeated-RM/RS code \(E\), decoder \(D\), and the declared ideal-stream fixed-weight sampling law. For uniform 128-bit \(m\), put \(F=\{D(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e))\ne m\}\). Let the explicit bound parameter \(B_{\rm model}\) be fixed by the full formula below: its coordinate parameter comes from uniform fixed supports, with finite RM error/tie bounds, RS correction radius, deterministic-tie correction and actual sampler-density factor all retained. The claim is \(\Pr[F]\le B_{\rm model}\). This compares one decoder event with an explicit bound; it does not claim that the residual coordinates are independent.

Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), truncation \(\pi_L\), and the specified repeated-RM/RS encoder and decoder \(E,D\). For a uniform 128-bit message and vectors with weights \(w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e\), define

\[
F(m,x,y,r_1,r_2,e)=\mathbf1\!\left[D\!\left(E(m)+\pi_L(xr_2+r_1y+e)\right)\ne m\right].
\]

This is the honest message-decoding failure event. Cancellation in the public equations gives exactly the displayed residual. Failure is averaged over honest messages and fresh keys; no supremum over maliciously chosen messages is taken. A retained decoder rejection is a failure. Native process crashes or invalid-generation operational errors are tracked separately, not discarded as successful observations.

\(\mathcal D_{\rm seed}\) is the actual finite-seed honest sampling law: it includes the public key seed, SHA3/SHAKE expansions, uniform message and salt, and the actual derivation of the encryption seed from those values. In particular it does not silently replace the concrete \(G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) encryption seed by a new independent draw. \(\mathcal D_{\rm ideal}\) replaces the declared honest expansion outputs by independent uniform expansion streams, consistently reused on repeated inputs, while retaining the same samplers, their bounds, the codec and its tie rules. The key sampler uses rejection for uniform fixed weight; the encryption sampler uses its specified fixed-work 32-bit procedure and retains that procedure's bias. No resampling is conditioned on successful decryption.

Here is the complete bound being claimed. Let \(n_1=16+2\delta\), repetition \(r\), and

\[
a=\sum_{\substack{j\text{ odd}}}\frac{\binom wj\binom{n-w}{w_r-j}}{\binom n{w_r}},\qquad
p=2a(1-a)(1-w_e/n)+(a^2+(1-a)^2)w_e/n.
\]

This \(p\) is the one-coordinate marginal for independent uniform fixed supports. It alone does not determine the tail of the correlated residual. The surrogate substitutes independent Bernoulli coordinates. For a repeated RM block let \(d=64r\), and take binomial coefficients outside their valid range to be zero. Define the finite weight counts

\[
b_i=\min\!\left\{2\binom{2d}i,\ 255\binom d{d/2}\binom d{i-d/2}
+510\sum_{j=d/2+1}^{d}\binom dj\binom d{i-j}
+\binom{255}{2}\sum_{j=0}^{d/2}\binom{d/2}j^3\binom{d/2}{i-d+j}\right\}.
\]

The inner error majorant and tie majorant are

\[
\pi=\frac12\sum_{i=0}^{2d}b_i p^i(1-p)^{2d-i},\qquad
\tau=\min\!\left\{1,255\binom d{d/2}[p(1-p)]^{d/2}\right\}.
\]

With \(\beta=(1+n/2^{32})^{2w_r+w_e}\), the complete outer expression is

\[
B_{\rm model}=\min\!\left\{1,\beta\left[\sum_{j=\delta+1}^{n_1}\binom{n_1}j\pi^j(1-\pi)^{n_1-j}
+\binom{n_1}{17}\tau^{17}\right]\right\}.
\]

The retained calculation rounds \(p\) upward to a 64-bit dyadic grid after checking the finite majorant's monotonicity, then rounds \(\pi,\tau\) upward to 256-bit dyadics. The rest is exact rational arithmetic. These conservative values, not unrounded floating approximations, define the bound in the premise. The final term handles the stated deterministic-tie coupling for uniform 16-byte RS messages; \(\beta\) retains the fixed-work encapsulation sampler's density adjustment.

statements.label: A-27
statements.title: Seeded noisy-product message recovery
statements.definition: Fix \(R=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\), an injective 128-bit message code \(E\) of length \(L\le n\), and public seed maps \(S_K,H_X,S_R\). From independent uniform 256-bit seeds obtain \((\alpha,x,y)=S_K(\sigma)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\), with weights \((w,w,w_r,w_r,w_e)\). Draw \(m\) uniformly from 128 bits. Publish \(\alpha,s=x+hy,u=r_1+hr_2,v=E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e)\), where \(\pi_L\) truncates to \(L\) coefficients. The claim is \(\Pr[A(\alpha,s,u,v)=m]\le\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T)\) for every classical algorithm of bit-RAM work at most \(T\). The seed maps and claimed success bound are parameters, not implicit uniformity or security guarantees.

statements.label: A-28
statements.title: Key-and-coins hash transfer
statements.definition: Fix the ring encryption map \(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta)=(r_1+hr_2,E(m)+\pi_L(sr_2+e))\), where \(P=(\alpha,s=x+hy)\), \(h=H_X(\alpha)\), and \((r_1,r_2,e)=S_R(\theta)\). Generate \(P\) by the declared key seed map; draw independent uniform 128-bit \(m,z\). Set \((K,\theta)=G(H(P)\Vert m\Vert z)\) and \(C=(\mathcal E(P,m;\theta),z)\). Let \(p_{\rm real}(T,Q)\) be the best classical probability of recovering \(K\) from \((P,C)\) with work \(T\) and \(Q\) calls to domain-separated SHA3-512 role \(G\). Define \(p_{\rm ideal}\) with only \(G\) replaced by an independent random function to 512 bits. The claim is \(p_{\rm real}\le p_{\rm ideal}+\delta_{\rm hash}(T,Q)\); no small slack is proved.

statements.label: A-32
statements.title: Almost every public key has a unique small secret
statements.definition:
Under the actual seeded key generator, at most one in 64 public keys has a different pair of weight-w secrets that explains the same public relation. An ideal random-multiplier calculation strongly motivates this premise, but does not prove it for fixed SHAKE.

Applies to Stages 1–66.

statements.label: A-33
statements.title: Enough information sets remain invertible
statements.definition:
For at least seven eighths of honest targets, at least one eighth of the selected column sets that contain the true error support give an invertible matrix. This is a working hypothesis about the actual structured public matrices; it has not been established for every stage. The curve is conditional on it.

Applies to Stages 4–66.

statements.label: A-34
statements.title: The stated decoding-failure bound applies to the actual scheme
statements.definition:
The scheme's conditional correctness analysis must bound actual honest decoding failure by 2^-128, including correlated ring errors and the chosen tie rule. Its surrogate-to-real-noise premise is still unproved for these research stages.

Applies to Stages 5–66.

statements.label: Security claim
statements.title: Passive shared-key recovery bound
statements.definition:
For every registered native configuration of exact research release `hqc@modeled-research-v3`, generate one fresh honest public key and one encapsulation. Let R be the supremum probability, among classical adversaries using at most T total computation work and the stated query budgets, of returning the complete 256-bit shared key in one output. Probability includes honest generation, encapsulation and the adversary's coins; condition on valid successful generation. Pre-challenge computation and designated hash queries count toward the same budgets.

\[R\le\min\{1,q_G\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T_B)+2^{-256}+\delta_{\rm hash}(T,q_G)\}.\]

\(\epsilon_{\rm PKE}(T_B)\) bounds the greatest success, at work \(T_B\), of recovering uniform 128-bit \(m\) from \((pk,\mathsf{Encrypt}(pk,m;\theta))\) with independent uniform 256-bit \(\theta\) and the exact native key distribution, seed maps, biased samplers and codec. \(q_G\) bounds distinct queries to the domain-separated \(G\) role. \(T_B\) includes the adversary, public digest/salt handling and lazy-table simulation. \(\delta_{\rm hash}(T,q_G)\) bounds excess recovery when concrete SHA3-512 role \(G\) replaces an independent random function to 512 bits; other hash/expansion roles remain fixed. The actual encapsulation uses its specified public salt and coupled key/coins derivation.

No decapsulation, key-checking or leakage oracle is available. The bounds concern a single classical target; they do not assert CCA, quantum or multi-target security. The success/advantage bounds and hash-transfer slack are explicit parameters, not numerically certified small values.

statements.label: Correctness claim
statements.title: Honest decoding and key agreement
statements.definition:
For every registered native configuration of exact research release `hqc@modeled-research-v3`, run honest \((pk,sk)\leftarrow\mathsf{KeyGen}\), \((C,K)\leftarrow\mathsf{Encaps}(pk)\) and \(K'=\mathsf{Decaps}(sk,C)\) using its specified samplers, mathematical algorithms, exact arithmetic and canonical encodings. Condition on valid successful key generation and completed operations, never on agreement.

The claim is \(\Pr[K'\ne K]\le d\), averaged over the honest keys and encapsulation randomness, with \(d=d_j\), where
\[d_j=\begin{cases}0&j=1,2,3,4,\\2^{-128}&j=5,6,\ldots,66.\end{cases}\]
where j identifies the corresponding frozen native tuple in this release's progression.

The same bound also applies to failure to recover the entire native message. Where the bound is zero, agreement holds for every allowed honest draw. Positive bounds concern the average honest experiment, not each key individually.

These are mathematical statements about the specified algorithms. They exclude invalid inputs, entropy or implementation faults, runtime aborts and side channels; they do not certify native executable correctness.

statements.label: Reference claim
statements.title: The earlier reference and remaining cryptanalysis — stated conclusion
statements.definition:
**Unquantified reference.** The earlier catalogue supplied no calibrated attack-cost curve for these 66 tuples. The elementary bit-RAM attacks below now provide explicit conditional work bounds. Competitive best-known attack estimates still require further cryptanalysis.

The October 2026 specification changes weights and other construction details. The retained August 2025 release cannot inherit the newer assessment, and conditional correctness is not a confidentiality estimate. An alternative low-weight solution to one public equation need not yield the target key; each attack must include its actual success argument and final key derivation.

**Scope.** Exact research release hqc@modeled-research-v3; classical model hqc2025-endpoint-reassessment-v1 (qualitative). Retain the source's qualifications; this is not converted into a current comparable bit-RAM estimate. This entry does not supply a complete quantified attack guarantee in the common computation model.
